specificFindings: The first-job and parenting questions are milestones for reflection,not instructions to change jobs or assessments of a childs performance. The first-job question is an elliptical continuation of the preceding question.

James formula and its pretentions spelling match the actual PDF. The text explicitly defines pretentions as aspirations;the success numerator and the two proposed routes are not reversed. Applying the formula to happiness is presented as a possible extreme simplification,not an established complete model of all psychological experience.
Likely succeeded retains the strength of the authors claim. Job satisfaction is one self-report based way to define work success,and the predictor question is not transformed into proof of causation.

Occupation figures are kept distinct:80 and78 percent satisfaction for actuaries and computer scientists,65 for police and59 for social workers. The authors pay explanation uses might and perhaps and is not represented as the only proven cause.

Payscale measured meaning as a separate item from satisfaction. The36 and45 percent meaning figures are not swapped with the satisfaction figures;the73 and81 figures belong to social workers and law enforcement. Group percentages do not imply every individual responds alike.

The editorial example keeps65 percent satisfaction and42 percent meaning. Funeral directors compare68 percent satisfaction and87 percent meaning. The conditional career recommendation is hypothetical,not a directive to learners.

The author cites self-expression and creativity as reasons not to make the hypothetical recommendation. The following source says Payscale did not ask about creativity;the explanation therefore attributes the comparison to the author rather than making an unsupported claim about every funeral director.
